issues_detected.description: Internal tension inside the regulatory_restrictions block: the nested regulatory_restrictions list asserts 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual instances', while the sibling other_compliance field in the same block records a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against court orders and subpoenas, mandatory administrative/physical/technical safeguards, a five-business-day breach-reporting duty and PhysioNet-specific requirements, and confidentiality_level is 'restricted' with hipaa_compliant 'compliant'. A reader cannot tell from the block alone whether regulatory constraints apply.
issues_detected.recommendation: Narrow the negative statement to its intended scope (e.g. 'No export-control restrictions apply') so it does not contradict the Certificate of Confidentiality, HIPAA and PhysioNet obligations recorded in other_compliance.

issues_detected.description: confidential_elements_present is set to false on the grounds that the dataset contains no data protected by legal privilege or doctor-patient confidentiality, yet the same entry's source_caveats records that 'the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality', and the release carries clinician-assigned diagnostic labels derived from clinical interviews and electronic health records. The boolean and the caveat point in opposite directions.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either set confidential_elements_present to true and scope the detail to the de-identified release, or state explicitly that the flag refers only to the released feature tables and not to the underlying clinical source data.

issues_detected.description: keywords contains only four terms ('health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'). Searchability is materially weaker than the record's own content warrants.
issues_detected.recommendation: Expand keywords to at least eight to twelve terms covering modality (speech, cough, respiratory sounds), conditions (voice disorders, neurodegenerative, psychiatric, respiratory, pediatric), methods (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning) and standards (BIDS).

issues_detected.description: variables lists only four entries (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), all of them generic columns of the feature Parquet files. issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period while the IRB protocol in the same source bundle describes a four-year phased study, with pilot collection begun November 2023 and ongoing November 2024. The record flags the tension itself in source_caveats and states which source it preferred and why, so the discrepancy is disclosed rather than concealed, but it remains unresolved.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet prefix 10.13026, which is consistent with the page URL (physionet.org), the citation ('PhysioNet'), the maintainers block (MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology) and the credentialed-access model described in data_governance - five independent fields agreeing on the same publishing platform.

Version identity is coherent across six fields: version 3.1.0, page path /b2ai-voice/3.1.0/, citation '(version 3.1.0)', version_access listing 3.1.0 with its own DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, errata describing what 3.1.0 fixed, and distribution_dates giving 1 May 2026 which matches issued.

The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type and is reasoned about rather than asserted: HIPAA Safe Harbor is supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and the record states plainly that 'K-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved' and that voice is inherently re-identifying - which is exactly why raw audio is withheld from the registered-access tier and routed through Synapse under DACO review. The two-tier access model follows from the stated risk rather than sitting beside it.

The human-subjects chain is complete end to end: involves_human_subjects true, USF single IRB with subsite engagement, SickKids REB for the pediatric cohort, an ethics working group memorandum, informed_consent with four consent modalities and a withdrawal mechanism, consent_revocations stating the post-collection limit on withdrawal, at_risk_populations with guardian consent and age-graded assent, and participant_compensation with amounts and caps.

Bias documentation uses BiasTypeEnum-aligned categories (representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) and each category is tied to a concrete mechanism in this dataset - five North American sites and English-only fluency for representation, trust and proximity for selection, per-site device configuration for measurement, single-labeler diagnosis for annotation - rather than generic bias language.

The record discloses shortfalls against the consortium's own AI-readiness scorecard as a limitation (data quality under characterization, domain-appropriate and associated criteria under sustainability, contextualized under computability), which is self-critical documentation rather than promotional reporting.

Software that actually produced the released artifacts is named throughout: b2aiprep converted raw waveforms into the Parquet feature files, sparc produced articulatory traces, openSMILE the acoustic features, Parselmouth and Praat the phonetic and prosodic features, ppgs the posteriorgrams and Whisper Large the transcriptions - each tied to the specific released feature family it generated.

The scope limitation is honest about what the registered-access release cannot support: 'Tasks that require the raw waveform, or that depend on free-speech content, cannot be performed with the registered-access release alone', and this matches the content_warnings entry recording that free-speech transcripts and spectrogram-family features were removed.

The record carries a dedicated top-level source_caveats resolving referent, counts, grant renderings, consortium size, enrollment target and two investigator name spellings, and states which source was preferred in each case - provenance discipline well above the norm for generated datasheets.

Grant identifiers OT2OD032720 and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 match NIH patterns (OT2 activity code, OD institute, six-digit serial; supplement type prefix 3 with -01S1 suffix) and are consistent with the stated NIH Common Fund grantor and the Bridge2AI program named in keywords and description.

sub_elements.quality_note: The preprocessing account is replicable at parameter level - window, hop, FFT size, sample rate, coefficient counts, frame rates - which is well beyond naming a pipeline. Annotation quality is addressed candidly on both limbs: a single annotator per item, and an explicit statement that the machine annotations have not been audited.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Parameters are internally coherent (25 ms window and 10 ms hop at 16 kHz correspond to a 400-point FFT, as stated). The single-annotator disclosure reappears as known_biases.annotation_bias and as a methodological known_limitation. imputation_protocols is unused as a slot, but missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'no imputation is applied', so the concept is documented; recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Element 8's datasets-shared condition is satisfied, and the dataset was processed (preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies and labeling_strategies are populated). Per the instrument, this sub-element is not gated on whether a repository pointer exists; the software-output condition governs sub-element 3 only.
sub_elements.evidence: Software that produced or transformed the released data, named across three slots. preprocessing_strategies prose: 'Articulatory features were generated with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package'; 'Acoustic features were extracted with openSMILE, and phonetic and prosodic features ... were computed with Parselmouth and Praat'; 'Phonetic posteriorgrams ... were generated with the ppgs package'; 'Transcriptions were generated using OpenAI's Whisper Large model.' machine_annotation_tools.tools: 'OpenAI Whisper Large', with tool_descriptions 'Used to generate transcriptions of the audio recordings during preprocessing.' external_resources: 'sensein/b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, convert the raw audio waveforms into the Parquet feature files and merge the source data into the phenotype files, at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep' (Apache-2.0), and 'sensein/senselab, the toolkit used for processing audio files for research tasks, at https://github.com/sensein/senselab'.
sub_elements.quality_note: The threshold is met decisively and in the right role. Each named tool is tied to the specific released artifact it produced: sparc to the articulatory traces, openSMILE to the static acoustic features, Parselmouth and Praat to the phonetic and prosodic measures, ppgs to the posteriorgrams, Whisper to the transcriptions, and b2aiprep to the Parquet conversion and phenotype merge that constitute the release itself. This is production and transformation software, not capture, hosting, packaging or validation tooling. Versions are largely absent (BIDS v1.9.0 and the Whisper 'Large' size are the only version-like qualifiers), which weakens reproducibility, but the sub-element asks whether the tooling is disclosed and it is, with two repositories and a licence each.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The evidence slots are preprocessing_strategies, machine_annotation_tools and external_resources. Note that the capture-side software also named in the record (the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, ReproSchema-UI, REDCap) falls under role (a), instrumentation, and PhysioNet and Synapse under role (b), hosting; neither was counted toward this score. The point rests solely on the derivation tooling. b2aiprep is corroborated as the release-producing library by extension_mechanism.contribution_url pointing to the same repository.

sub_elements.name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: six entries with URLs, licences and two Zenodo archival DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.12760724 for the REDCap dictionary, 10.5281/zenodo.13834653 for the documentation), plus the FHIR profiles and the Scholars training programme. conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. Imputation: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'A missingness table is generated as part of the audit protocol and is included with the dataset; no imputation is applied.'
sub_elements.quality_note: External standards and supporting resources are extensive and, importantly, archived - two of the repositories carry Zenodo DOIs, so the documentation a reuser needs will outlive the GitHub URLs. The imputation question is answered explicitly in the negative, which is the documentation the criterion asks for even though the dedicated slot is unused.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Zenodo DOIs use the correct 10.5281 prefix. The archival true flags match the entries that carry Zenodo DOIs, and are absent from the entries that do not - an internally consistent use of the flag. The 'no imputation' statement is consistent with cleaning_strategies ('No pre-processing was performed to clean the data').

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries - representativeness_limitation (with recommended_mitigation 'Assess the multivariate distribution of disorder category, site and demographics before using the data for a given question'); coverage_limitation ('Data collection was conducted in English only; participants who do not read or speak English were excluded'); temporal_limitation ('changes in diagnostic criteria or practices during the collection period could alter how labels were assigned'); scope_limitation (derived features rather than original recordings, with scope_impact 'Tasks that require the raw waveform, or that depend on free-speech content, cannot be performed with the registered-access release alone'); and two methodological_limitation entries covering single-labeler diagnosis and the consortium's own AI-readiness shortfalls.
sub_elements.quality_note: Six limitations, each typed, each specific to this dataset, and several carrying a mitigation or an explicit statement of what analyses become impossible. The final entry discloses failure against the consortium's own readiness criteria - self-critical reporting that most datasheets omit.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: representativeness by sampling_strategies.is_representative false, coverage by why_not_representative, scope by distribution_formats and the 2.0.0 erratum, methodological by labeling_strategies.annotations_per_item 1. No limitation is asserted without a supporting fact in the record.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries with bias_type values representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias. representation_bias carries a mitigation_strategy ('shift to remote collection ... and to expand data collection to Spanish'); measurement_bias carries affected_subsets ('Disease cohorts recruited at distinct recording sites'); selection_bias identifies the mechanism ('Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites'); annotation_bias describes the varying diagnostic basis across cohorts. future_use_impacts supplies the social-impact limb: the skew warning and 'risks of voice re-identification, vulnerabilities such as voice AI hacking, concerns around voice data sharing and privacy, and the influence of gender and racial diversity on the development and application of these technologies.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Four BiasTypeEnum-aligned categories, each tied to a concrete mechanism operating in this specific collection rather than to generic fairness language, and two of the four carry structured mitigation or affected-subset detail. The anticipated downstream social impacts required by the RAI alignment are present in future_use_impacts.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The bias_type values match the enumerated taxonomy the criterion names. Each bias is traceable to a documented collection fact: measurement_bias to the per-site device configurations in collection_mechanisms and anomalies, annotation_bias to labeling_strategies, representation_bias to sampling_strategies.why_not_representative. Taxonomy use is substantive rather than decorative.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: 'Different sites have different collection configurations, and the collection protocol changed over the course of the study'; 'Possible sources of noise and error include recording noise artifacts, variations in diagnostic practices between sites and clinicians, inaccurate questionnaire responses, and underreporting'; 'Some audio files could not generate certain features, whether because of length or other issues, and are therefore missing from the corresponding Parquet feature files.' cleaning_strategies documents the audit protocol that surfaces such issues, including silence and duration metrics and comparison of produced speech against the intended passage.
sub_elements.quality_note: Three distinct anomaly classes - protocol drift, measurement and reporting noise, and extraction failures - and the third has a direct operational consequence for anyone loading the Parquet files, which the record states rather than leaving to discovery.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The feature-extraction failure anomaly explains the per-feature count divergence reported in source_caveats (32,522 pitch series against 29,278 spectrograms), so the anomaly and the counts corroborate each other. Protocol drift is consistent with the temporal_limitation and with errata describing reprocessing across versions.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: four entries flagging race and ethnic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information, and 'The raw voice recordings are themselves sensitive, because a voice has the potential to cause individual re-identification or to be used for illicit or unauthorized purposes; for this reason all raw voice data were removed from the registered-access release.' content_warnings: content_warnings_present true, with a warning about free speech tasks ('while offensive, insulting or threatening content is unlikely, it cannot be completely avoided because research participants are responsible for their choice of language') and a note that the risk is reduced in the released set because free-speech transcripts and derived spectrogram-family features were removed. confidential_elements is also populated.
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive categories are enumerated, and the voice-as-biometric sensitivity is treated as a first-class item with its consequence for the release stated. The content warning is proportionate rather than alarmist and explains how the release mitigates the risk.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The content_warnings source_caveats resolves a genuine conflict between sources about whether free-speech transcripts are included, states which source was preferred and why ('the PhysioNet statement is the more recent and higher-ranked source'), and the resolution agrees with the 2.0.0 erratum and the scope_limitation. Flagged separately: confidential_elements_present false sits in tension with the Certificate of Confidentiality recorded in its own caveat, an issue recorded against Element 2's evidence.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: three entries (USF IRB, SickKids REB, Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group, the last having 'produced a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples, which is published alongside the dataset documentation'). future_use_impacts: 'The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors; future users should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility, to avoid uses that could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups'; and 'The consortium recognizes growing ethical, legal and social challenges surrounding voice AI, including risks of voice re-identification, vulnerabilities such as voice AI hacking, concerns around voice data sharing and privacy, and the influence of gender and racial diversity on the development and application of these technologies.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both limbs are met and they connect: the ethics working group's analysis of voice re-identification risk is the reason for the access architecture, and future_use_impacts extends that analysis to downstream societal risks including discriminatory use and adversarial misuse. This is anticipatory impact analysis rather than a compliance statement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The social-impact content is consistent with discouraged_uses (hiring, insurance, surveillance) and with prohibited_uses (harm and stigmatization), so the impact analysis is operationalized as use restrictions rather than left as commentary. Conflicts of interest are not addressed, a minor gap against the criterion's fuller scope; the ethical review and social impact limbs are both substantively present.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied: distribution_formats populated with access_urls to physionet.org and synapse.org; licence permits research reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: The publisher slot is unused, but the platform is identified unambiguously in four other fields: citation ends 'PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; maintainers records 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, hosts the current dataset versions and administers credentialed access' and 'The Health Data Nexus, a data publishing platform maintained by the Temerty Center for Artificial Intelligence Research and Education in Medicine (T-CAIREM) based at the University of Toronto'; third_party_sharing states distribution 'through the PhysioNet data publishing platform under registered and credentialed access, and through Synapse for the raw audio'; page resolves to physionet.org.

A reader can determine the publishing platform, its operator, the credentialing regime it administers, the separate controlled-access host, and the earlier host - more than the criterion asks for. The absence of the dedicated publisher slot is a serialization gap recorded as a low-severity issue, not an absence of the information the sub-element seeks.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: PhysioNet is corroborated as publisher by the 10.13026 DOI prefix, by the page domain, by the citation and by the RRID SCR_007345, which is PhysioNet's own resource identifier. Four-way agreement; the platform attribution is not in doubt.

Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. external_resources adds 'Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, published by the consortium as supporting material'. labeling_strategies uses ICD-10; instances use B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE identifiers.
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance spans a versioned data-organization standard, a resolvable metadata schema, a clinical terminology, ontology identifiers and a clinical interoperability profile. The consortium is also contributing standards back to the community via the FHIR profiles, which is integration in both directions.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: BIDS v1.9.0 is a real versioned release and is appropriate to the participant/session directory organization described in distribution_formats. The FHIR profile reference is honest about its own incompleteness ('does not give a repository URL in the captured text'). All conformance claims are corroborated by the preprocessing account, which describes the BIDS conversion step.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources includes 'eipm/bridge2ai-docs, the source code for the Bridge2AI-Voice documentation and dashboards published at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, archived on Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653' and 'Training opportunities for using the dataset are offered through the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars program at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/'. page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. existing_uses records prior use in 'the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation site, dashboards, an archived documentation snapshot, a named training programme with its own URL, and evidence of prior educational use. This covers the outreach limb well beyond a bare documentation link.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well formed and the domains (docs.b2ai-voice.org, b2aivoicescholars.org) are consistent with the project identity and with the DACO contact domain b2ai-voice.org. The Zenodo archival DOI carries the correct 10.5281 prefix and matches the archival true flag on that entry.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: 'is_supplemented_by' -> doi:10.13026/h995-bt35, Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, described with its own REB approval, protocol, contents ('Version 1.1.0 contains derived audio features for 23,533 recordings collected from 300 participants aged 2 to 18') and latest-version DOI 10.13026/mf9s-5r03; 'is_new_version_of' -> doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84, version 1.0 on the Health Data Nexus, 'which provides cloud compute alongside the dataset rather than allowing data downloads'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both relationships carry an explicit type, a resolvable DOI, a name and a description substantive enough that a user can decide whether the related dataset is relevant without resolving the link. The pediatric entry even carries its own counts and governance context.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly: the pediatric cohort supplements rather than supersedes, and version 1.0 on a different platform is properly typed as a prior version. Both targets are corroborated elsewhere in the record - the pediatric dataset by human_subject_research.special_populations and ethical_reviews, and version 1.0 by version_access and maintainers.

strengths: Ethics and privacy documentation is complete end to end and internally reasoned: the record states that k-anonymity of 2 or more is not achieved and that voice is inherently re-identifying, and then derives the two-tier access model from that finding rather than asserting safety - IRB, REB, ethics working group, consent modalities, withdrawal limits, assent thresholds and compensation caps are all specified.

Preprocessing is documented at parameter level (16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth filter, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 MFCCs, 50 Hz articulatory traces, 100 Hz posteriorgrams over 40 units) with the producing software named per feature family - sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large and the b2aiprep conversion library.

Version and provenance tracking is exemplary: six releases enumerated with dates, per-version DOIs, per-version errata naming breaking changes such as renamed gold standard variables, a stated semi-annual cadence corroborated by the observed release history, and an explicit retention policy for superseded versions.

Limitations and biases are disclosed self-critically, including four BiasTypeEnum-aligned categories each tied to a concrete collection mechanism, and a limitation entry recording the dataset's failures against the consortium's own AI-readiness criteria.

A dedicated top-level source_caveats block adjudicates referent, participant and recording counts, grant identifier renderings, consortium size, enrollment target and investigator name spellings, stating in each case which source was preferred and why - provenance discipline well above the norm for generated datasheets.
weaknesses: Variable-level metadata is token: four generic feature-file columns are documented while the phenotype tables the record itself enumerates - confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires, task metadata - have no variable descriptions, and is_tabular is unset for an all-tabular release.

Keywords number only four and cover domain and programme only, omitting the modalities, conditions, methods and standards that the description enumerates, so the dataset is far less discoverable than its content warrants.

The regulatory_restrictions block contradicts itself: its nested list asserts that no regulatory restrictions apply while the sibling other_compliance field records a Certificate of Confidentiality, HIPAA safeguards, a breach-reporting duty and PhysioNet requirements, with confidentiality_level set to restricted.

confidential_elements_present is false while the same entry's caveat records a Certificate of Confidentiality over the underlying data and the release carries clinician-assigned diagnoses, leaving the flag at odds with its own annotation.

Several dedicated schema slots are unused where the information exists in prose - publisher, download_url, data_governance.committee_contact, imputation_protocols, data_protection_impacts, was_derived_from - which costs machine-readability even though a human reader loses nothing.
recommendations: Extend variables to cover the phenotype table columns, or at minimum one representative block per table, and set is_tabular; reference the shipped JSON data dictionaries as the authoritative full list.

Expand keywords to eight to twelve terms covering modality (speech, cough, respiratory sounds), the five disease cohorts, methods (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram, acoustic biomarkers) and standards (BIDS, FHIR).

Narrow the negative statement in regulatory_restrictions to export controls specifically, so it no longer contradicts the Certificate of Confidentiality and safeguard duties in other_compliance, and reconcile confidential_elements_present with that certificate.

Populate the dedicated slots that already have prose backing: publisher ('PhysioNet, MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology'), data_governance.committee_contact (DACO@b2ai-voice.org), an imputation_protocols entry recording that no imputation was applied, and a data_protection_impacts entry pointing to the ethics working group memorandum.

Record software versions alongside the named tools (openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, sparc, ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab) and pin the b2aiprep release used for this version, so the parameter-level preprocessing account becomes fully reproducible.

State character encoding for the TSV distributions and MIME media types for each distribution_format entry, and resolve the collection_timeframes 12-month figure into an explicit date range related to the wider four-year study period.
